Welcome to My Cybersecurity Portfolio

Hello! Welcome to my cybersecurity portfolio. This website documents my learning journey, practical cybersecurity projects, technical skills, and development as a future cybersecurity professional.

I am currently pursuing a Master of Cybersecurity at Universiti Malaya, where I am developing my knowledge and practical skills in cybersecurity.

My main interests include Network Security, Penetration Testing, Ethical Hacking, Cloud Security, and IoT Security.

About Me

My name is Yong Yi Heng, and I am currently pursuing a Master of Cybersecurity at Universiti Malaya, which I started in September 2026 and expect to complete in 2028.

Before beginning my postgraduate studies, I completed a Bachelor of Computer Science (Hons), majoring in Cloud Computing, at INTI International University, with a CGPA of 3.43/4.00. I was also a Dean’s Award recipient throughout my semesters.

My academic background in computer science and cloud computing has provided me with a foundation in programming, software development, and computing technologies. I am now expanding that foundation into cybersecurity through academic learning and practical laboratory exercises.

I enjoy exploring technical challenges, learning new technologies, and applying what I learn through hands-on projects. My long-term goal is to become a Cloud Security Engineer.

Projects

This section showcases my practical cybersecurity projects. Each project includes its objectives, laboratory environment, methodology, findings, and supporting evidence.

1. Virtual Lab Setup: Kali Linux and Metasploitable 2

Objective: To establish an isolated virtual cybersecurity laboratory for practising network security and penetration-testing activities.

Tools and Technologies:

  • Kali Linux
  • Metasploitable 2
  • UTM Virtual Machine
  • Virtual Networking

Key Activities:

  • Set up Kali Linux and Metasploitable 2 as virtual machines.
  • Configure the virtual network environment.
  • Troubleshoot network connectivity between the two virtual machines.
  • Verify communication between the attacker and target machines.
  • Maintain an isolated laboratory environment for safe testing.

View Project 1

2. Nmap Network Scanning and Service Detection

Objective: To identify open ports and running services on a target virtual machine using Nmap.

Tools and Technologies:

  • Kali Linux
  • Metasploitable 2
  • Nmap
  • UTM Virtual Machine

Key Activities:

  • Verify network connectivity between Kali Linux and Metasploitable 2.
  • Perform a basic Nmap network scan.
  • Use service version detection to identify running services.
  • Save scan results for documentation and analysis.
  • Examine potential security risks associated with exposed services.

Key Learning Outcome:

This project helped me understand how network scanning can reveal exposed services and potential areas of security concern. I also learned that identifying an open port does not automatically prove that a system is vulnerable.

Learning Journey

My cybersecurity learning journey is an ongoing process of developing my theoretical knowledge and practical technical skills. Although my previous academic background focused on Computer Science and Cloud Computing, I am now expanding my knowledge into cybersecurity through my Master of Cybersecurity programme at Universiti Malaya, which I started in September 2026.

Throughout my studies, I have been introduced to different cybersecurity topics through courses such as Cyber Security and Advanced Computer Penetration and Defence. These courses have helped me understand cybersecurity from both theoretical and practical perspectives.

One interesting experience from my Cyber Security course is the attendance activity. Instead of simply providing an attendance password, the lecturer gives students different tasks and challenges that require us to discover the password independently. This encourages me to think critically, investigate the given tasks, and apply my problem-solving skills rather than simply following instructions. It has also helped me understand the importance of curiosity and independent learning in cybersecurity.

For Advanced Computer Penetration and Defence, the lecturer provides practical laboratory exercises and tutorials to help us strengthen our technical knowledge. These activities allow me to practise using cybersecurity tools and understand how different penetration-testing techniques work. Both courses involve some similar tools and practical activities, which gives me more opportunities to become familiar with the tools through repeated practice.

Outside the classroom, I have also completed two practical projects. My first project involved setting up an isolated virtual cybersecurity laboratory using Kali Linux and Metasploitable 2 through UTM on macOS. During the setup process, I encountered difficulties configuring the network connection between the two virtual machines. Initially, they could not communicate with each other. I investigated the virtual network settings and discovered that the machines needed to use the same network environment. After configuring both machines to use Shared Network, I successfully established communication between them. This experience taught me the importance of understanding virtual networking and troubleshooting technical problems.

My second project focused on network scanning and service detection using Nmap. I performed basic scans and used the -sV option to identify services and their versions running on the target machine. Through this exercise, I learned how to identify open ports, interpret scanning results, and understand the potential security risks associated with exposed network services.

Although I have gained some practical experience, I still find it challenging to interpret network scanning results and understand the security implications of different services. I can identify open ports and service versions using Nmap, but I need more practice understanding how these services operate and how potential weaknesses can affect a system. I plan to improve this knowledge through additional laboratory exercises and independent research.

Moving forward, my improvement goal is to complete all the practical laboratories, tutorials, and learning activities assigned by my lecturers by 31 January 2027. I will measure my progress by tracking the number of assigned activities completed, ensuring that I can successfully perform the required tasks, and documenting my learning outcomes with screenshots and explanations. I also plan to continue my Cisco Networking Academy and TryHackMe learning activities to gain additional practical experience.

Overall, these learning experiences have helped me understand that cybersecurity requires continuous learning, independent problem-solving, and practical experience. I look forward to exploring more cybersecurity areas throughout my Master’s programme before deciding on my future career specialisation.

Career Objective

My career objective is to become a Cloud Security Engineer, focusing on protecting cloud infrastructure, applications, and data from cybersecurity threats.

With my academic background in Computer Science and Cloud Computing, together with my current postgraduate studies in Cybersecurity, I aim to combine my knowledge of cloud technologies with cybersecurity principles to develop secure and reliable computing environments.

I am particularly interested in cloud security architecture, network protection, access control, vulnerability assessment, and security monitoring. I understand that becoming a competent Cloud Security Engineer requires continuous learning and practical experience.

Therefore, I aim to strengthen my technical foundation through hands-on laboratories, cybersecurity projects, postgraduate studies, and relevant industry certifications. In the future, I hope to contribute to organisations by identifying security risks, improving cloud security practices, and protecting important digital assets.

However, as I am still in the process of expanding my knowledge of different cybersecurity areas, I also want to explore other specialisations, such as Network Security, Penetration Testing, Ethical Hacking, and IoT Security. After completing my postgraduate courses and gaining more practical experience, I will further evaluate my interests, strengths, and career opportunities before making a final decision about my professional specialisation.
